spans.s:
1. दिन, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. दिन see p. 412, col. 3),
cut, split, destroyed.
दिन 1. दिन. See rt. 3. दा, p. 408, col. 2.

दिन 2. दिन, अस्, अम्, m. n. (probably for
दिवन and related to 3. दिव् fr. rt. 2. दिव्, said to
be fr. rt. दो), a day; [cf. दुर्-द्˚, पुरु-द्˚, मध्-
यन्-द्˚, सु-द्˚; cf. also Lith. die†na, f. ‘a day;’
Slav. deny, ‘a day;’ Lat. peren-dinus, peren-dina-
tio, peren = para; perhaps Goth. sin-teins, ‘daily,’
sin = sam.]
—दिन-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, making day
or light; (ई), f., scil. टीका, N. of a commentary on
the Bhāṣā-pariccheda; (अस्), m. the sun; N. of
the author of the work Candrārkī.
—दिनकर-
तनय, अस्, m. ‘the son of the Sun,’ the planet
Saturn.
—दिनकर-देव, अस्, m., N. of a poet.
—दिनकरात्मजा (˚र-आत्˚), f. ‘the daughter of
the Sun,’ an epithet of the Yamunā or Jumnā river.
—दिन-कर्तृ, ता, m. or दिन-कृत्, त्, m. ‘the
day-maker,’ the sun.
—दिन-केशर or दिन-केसर
or दिन-केशव, अस्, m. ‘the hair of the day,’ the
darkness.
—दिन-क्षय, अस्, m. ‘the decline of
day,’ the evening, = तिथि-क्षय; N. of a chapter
in the Purāṇa-sarva-sva.
—दिन-ज्योतिस्, इस्, n. ‘day-
light,’ sunshine.
—दिन-दुःखित, अस्, आ, अम्, af-
flicted by day, sorrowing by day; (अस्), m. the bird
Cakra-vāka, the ruddy goose.
—दिन-नक्त, अम्,
n. day and night.
—दिन-पति, इस्, m. ‘the lord of
the day,’ the sun.
—दिन-प्रणी, ईस्, m. ‘the bringer
of day,’ the sun; [cf. तिथि-प्रणी.]
—दिन-बन्-
धु, उस्, m. ‘the friend of the day,’ the sun.
—दिन-
बल, अस्, m. ‘the strength of the day,’ N. of the
fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, eleventh, and twelfth
signs of the zodiac collectively.
—दिन-मणि, इस्,
m. ‘the jewel of day,’ the sun.
—दिन-मल, अम्, n.
‘day-refuse (?),’ a month.
—दिन-मूर्धन्, आ, m.
‘the head of the day,’ the eastern mountain behind
which the sun is supposed to rise; [cf. उदय.]
—दिन-रत्न, अम्, n. ‘the jewel of the day,’ the
sun.
—दिन-राशि, इस्, m. ‘the sum or collective
amount of days,’ i. e. the number of solar days
which have elapsed from one given point of time to
another.
—दिन-व्यास-दल, अम्, n. ‘half-diameter
or radius of the sky,’ i. e. the radius of a circle made
by an asterism in its daily revolution.
—दिनांश
(˚न-अंश), अस्, m. ‘any portion of a day,’ i. e. a
watch, an hour, morning, forenoon, afternoon, &c.
—दिनागम (˚न-आग्˚), अस्, m. day-break.
—दि-
नाण्ड (˚न-अण्ड?), अम्, n. ‘day-egg,’ i. e. dark-
ness, (the egg or embryo whence day proceeds.)
—दिनात्यय (˚न-अत्˚), अस्, m. ‘the decline of
day,’ evening.
—दिनादि (˚न-आदि), इस्, m. ‘day-
break,’ dawn.
—दिनाधीश (˚न-अध्˚), अस्, m.
‘the lord of day,’ the sun.
—दिनान्त (˚न-अन्˚),
अस्, m. ‘end of day,’ sun-set, evening.
—दिनान्तक
(˚न-अन्˚), अस्, m. ‘day-destroyer,’ darkness.
—दि-
नारम्भ (˚न-आर्˚), अस्, m. ‘day-break,’ morning.
—दिनार्ध (˚न-अर्˚), अस्, m. ‘the half of the
day,’ noon.
—दिनावसान (˚न-अव्˚), अम्, n. ‘close
of day,’ evening.
—दिनास्त्र (˚न-अस्˚), अम्, n.
‘day-missile,’ N. of a magical formula.
—दिनी-कृ,
cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to reduce
to days.
—दिनेश (˚न-ईश), अस्, m. ‘the lord of
day,’ the sun; the regent of a day.
—दिनेशात्मज
(˚श-आत्˚), अस्, m. ‘the son of the Sun,’ the planet
Mercury.
—दिनेश्वर (˚न-ईश्˚), अस्, m. ‘the lord
of the day,’ the sun.
—दिनैक (˚न-एक), अस्, m.
one day.

दीन, अस्, आ, अम्, scarce, scanty (Ved.); poor,
indigent, needy, afflicted, distressed, ruined, mise-
rable, wretched, dejected, downcast, melancholy;
frightened, afraid, timid [cf. परि-द्˚]; (अम्), n.
distress, wretchedness [cf. दैन्य]; the plant Ta-
bernæmontana Coronaria; (अम्), ind. miserably;
(आ), f. the female of a mouse or shrew.
—दीन-
चेतन, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘distressed or dejected in mind,’
distressed, dejected.
—दीन-ता, f. scarcity, rarity
(Ved.); wretchedness, distress, weakness.
—दीन-
दक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, of weak understanding.
—दीन-
दास, अस्, m. a name applied to a Śūdra.
—दीन-
धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, ‘having melancholy thoughts,’ de-
jected, helpless.
—दीन-मनस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, or दीन-
मानस, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘afflicted in mind,’ distressed,
dejected, downcast.
—दीन-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘hav-
ing a dejected countenance,’ of melancholy aspect.
—दीन-लोचन, अस्, m. a cat.
—दीन-वत्सल, अस्, आ,
अम्, kind to the poor.
—दीन-वदन = दीन-मुख.
—दीन-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘having a bad colour,’
discoloured.
—दीनानुकम्पन (˚न-अन्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, ‘compassionating the poor,’ kind to the poor.
दीन दीन, अस्, आ, अम्, See p. 415, col. 3.

दिनिका, f. a day's wages, hire for a day or by
the day.

दिन्नाग्राम दिन्ना-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a
village of the Khāśakas.

दीनक, अस्, आ, अम्, wretched, distressed; (अम्),
ind. in a wretched manner, miserably.

दीनार दीनार, अस्, m. (fr. the Gr. δηνάριον,
= देनरिउस्, said to be fr. rt. 3. दी), a coin, a
gold coin; a weight of gold (variously stated as 2
Kāṣṭhas, 1 Pala of 32 Rettis or the large Pala of
108 Su-varṇas); a gold ornament; a seal.
